title: aiPHeed: food-insecurity risk indicators for CALABARZON (DA Region IV-A)

served_engine.name: PCF21
served_engine.why_served: the only candidate that can issue 2026-Q4/2027-Q1 estimates from released data and the best model-based Brier score on development quarters; P45 (the researcher's primary candidate) needs 2026 government features that do not exist and did not do better on the unseen quarter
served_engine.evidence_status: EXPERIMENTAL (no lead validated against persistence and always-HIGH)

target_definition.label: T1: S1 = H + 2D > tau, HIGH or LOW (the approved Chapter I composite food-stress label)
target_definition.H: SWS Balance Luzon self-rated hunger (%), one regional value for all five provinces (measured)
target_definition.D: province food inflation minus the five-province mean (pp), PSA provincial CPI (measured)
target_definition.tau: median S1 of the published labelled quarters before the origin (trailing median)
target_definition.observable: after the quarter's SWS round is posted and its last CPI month is released (2026-Q3: 14 Oct 2026)
target_definition.is_not: an official or measured food-insecurity prevalence; provincial differences come only from prices

regional_hunger.what: SWS self-rated involuntary hunger, Balance Luzon (Luzon outside Metro Manila)
regional_hunger.geographic_level: regional: ONE value shared by all five provinces; not a provincial or municipal measurement

lgu_ranking.meaning: Indicative, relative ordering of the 142 cities and municipalities for planning attention. It is the province estimate re-weighted by PSA poverty incidence (60%) and PSA 2020 population density (40%) inside each province. It is not a measured municipal food-insecurity rate, not an independent municipal forecast and not an official classification (Chapter I, 1.7). The province estimate it starts from has NOT been validated against baselines (E25-E28), so the ranking inherits that status: EXPERIMENTAL.
does_not_mean: It does not say that any LGU is food insecure, or how many households are.
Positions across provinces mostly reflect the province estimate; positions inside a province reflect the vulnerability weights only.
For the 126 LGUs without a PSA municipal poverty estimate, the poverty term is a province-mean substitute, so their order inside the province comes from population density alone.
Two LGUs with equal risk_index share a rank; their listing order (PSGC) carries no meaning.

population_2020.source: PSA 2020 Census of Population and Housing (CPH)

poverty_lgu_estimate.source: PSA 2021 Small Area Estimates of Poverty (released 2024), as exported by E25

poverty_value_used.source: LGU estimate where published; otherwise the province value exported by E25

province_probability.source: the stored province estimate the ranking is computed from
province_probability.transformation: risk_index = probability x vulnerability, clamp [0,1], 4 dp

lgu_ranking.method: vulnerability = 0.6 x poverty_norm + 0.4 x density_norm (min-max within province); risk_index = province probability x vulnerability, clamp [0,1], 4 dp; competition ranks, ties by PSGC; null probability -> null risk and ranks

development_metrics_T1.basis: E28 frozen protocol d897f56d; walk-forward expanding window; every quarter had been examined before (development evidence)

PROPOSED_E25.label: P45: proposed LightGBM, 45 candidates (researcher's primary model)

unseen_quarter_2026Q3.caveat: ONE quarter, five rows that share one regional H: a single observation of regional hunger. No statistical claim of skill can rest on it; it is the first unseen-quarter data point.

threshold_75pct.source: the researcher's brief (E31); Chapter I itself states no numeric threshold

rows.arm: P45: proposed LightGBM, 45 candidates (researcher's primary model)

threshold_75pct.verdict: Several arms exceed 75% accuracy at lead 1, but so does always-HIGH (0.911) because 91% of test labels are HIGH. No arm beats persistence AND always-HIGH on accuracy or Brier, so accuracy above 75% does not show forecasting skill here; the requirement is met only in a form that a constant forecast also meets.

limitations: The label is 68% regional SWS hunger: one survey value drives all five provinces, so most quarters (and 2026-Q3) are HIGH everywhere. Provincial differences come only from relative food prices.
No lead time is validated: on development quarters no model beats persistence and always-HIGH; the unseen 2026-Q3 is one regional observation (five rows that share one H).

News evidence is title-only. The relevance rule R1 has precision 0.85 and estimated recall 0.40 on a blind holdout (deployed R1.1 fixes its false-positive patterns; not yet re-validated on fresh data), so most province-quarters still have limited or no news evidence.
126 of 142 LGUs use a province-mean poverty substitute (2021 municipal SAE extract not available without loading pre-2021 values); their order inside a province comes from population density.
Annotation of the relevance samples was done by the AI assistant, not by the researchers; a researcher re-review of validation/*/annotation_sheet_blind.json is recommended before thesis use.
Google News robots.txt disallows automated access to /rss for generic crawlers; continued use of this source needs the researcher's decision (see E31 FINAL_REPORT).
disclaimer: aiPHeed produces potential food-insecurity risk indicators for review. They are not official food-insecurity classifications and do not replace assessments by authorized government agencies.
